newsitem.title: CHINA: China life insurance grows 70 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China life insurance grows 70 pct in 1996.

text.p: China's total premium income generated from life insurance hit 33 billion yuan last year, an increase of 70 percent compared with 1995, statistics from the Ping'an Insurance Co showed on Tuesday.
About half of China's nearly 300 million urban residents have considered buying life insurance, the Xinhua news agency quoted He Zhiguang, deputy manager of the Ping'an Insurance Company, as saying.
The World Bank predicts that by 2000, the total income of China's insurance industry will reach 250 billion yuan, half from life insurance premium income, he said.

The per capita annual income of urban residents was about 4,500 yuan last year, which made life insurance more affordable as Beijing reshapes a social welfare system in a country where for years the state provided cradle-to-grave care.
"This creates a big life insurance market for both home and overseas insurers, and one which has kept growing at a double-digit rate over the past few years," He said.

Per capita spending on life insurance services of Chinese residents was no more than $1.4 last year, with the total premium income of life insurance accounting for less than 0.3 percent of gross national product, he said.

China now has five nationwide life insurers -- the giant People's Insurance Company of China, Pacific Ocean Insurance Co and Ping'an Insurance Co and the smaller New China and Taikang companies set up last year.
